messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: suggestions for doc or manual?  or citations?
parts:
Daniel and I are putting a bow on Stan 2.0, and we should
be distributing a release candidate next week.

If you have suggestions for the manual, please send e-mail
to this list, or better yet, add them to the appropriate issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/211

Thanks for the great suggestions that are already there. I took
everyone's advice, and I think it's a big improvement on clarity.

Also, if you have papers that cite Stan, we're including a list
on the new web pages. You can send mail here, or again, better
yet, add them to the appropriate issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/187

After 2.0, I think we're going to have standing issues for manual
corrections/suggestions and citations.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: suggestions for doc or manual?  or citations?
parts:
Yes, Jiqiang will have RStan 2.0 ready to go. We'll
roll out a release candidate of that first.

Allen Riddell's also polishing off PyStan, so we'll
also have a Python interface!

We still plan to do MATLAB sometimes in the next year or two,
and also have a proposal in the works for a Stata interface.
Coupled with all the C++ compilers and OS versions, it's
quite a bit of work on the integration side (and I'm not
talking about our Hamiltonian simulations).

- Bob

messages.author: 9d7e54e3329f305f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggestions for doc or manual?  or citations?
parts:
Super minor issue, but since you asked...

Looks like increment_log_prob() is not in Part V (Built-in Functions) of the 2.0 manual. Not a big deal since the function is explained in detail elsewhere, but it's nice to have all the functions in one place for reference. And I couldn't find its function signature anywhere in the existing doc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggestions for doc or manual?  or citations?
parts:
Thanks. The signature and function definition should
definitely be in Part V.

It's not really a function like the other functions --- for
example, there's no return value. But it should still be
discussed there and put in the index.

I opened a new doc issue for the next release:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/292

and added your comment so we'll remember to fix it.

- Bob
